searchText: Hello, would it be feasible for the EF to start nodes for checkpoint-sync and use them for "Bootstrap nodes"? I think that could improve UX by a lot as you would not need an external provider anymore or is it not feasible because of DDOS or something like that? I think the issue with that is more around centralization. We'd rather work on making it easier to set them up and discoverable as well as tooling to allow enough people to set them up themselves. afaik infura is the only checkpoint sync provider right now — added it to our todo 📝 Well, the power stands only when node is bootstraped, it is a difficult attack It would be nice to have a set of different providers offering some public bootstrap nodea Maybe on launch the node randomly chooses a provider But even if it is a single provider it seems a rather hard attack on decentralization My main concern is this: if we do not make it default then 90% of people running a node will run it through initial sync and rightfully so as that is the default syncing method which btw is unsafe to use in the first place, so i think it would not be an attack on decentralization, quite the opposite 🙂 it just seems a pretty easy and impactful improvement to the UX to me anyways, which got harder already. keep an eye on this repo from Sam😄 https://github.com/samcm/checkpointz The idea is for that to be a beacon node aware reverse proxy that allows just calls needed for checkpoint sync. Additionally you can configure caching to reduce the load on the node. that's a fair point. Our plan is to first get some tooling in place to run these nodes easily, then to make them visible and just act as a source of info. I guess we can talk about how to use that source of info once its up. cool, will this be available before the merge? That's the plan ™️ I wanted to write something like this in Rust darn it they preceded me 🙂 I don't see anything wrong with the provider being somewhat centralized, we only need to have several providers of the roots to check against it is quite easy if you use this as you could just use an Infure key for one provider, an EF node for another provider, etc... I think we would want something like this before mainnet That's kinda the idea 😄 We'd like some endpoints from client teams sourced there as well. I think the idea we had for the project is summarized here: https://twitter.com/parithosh_j/status/1552730345346310152 okay i see, i hope it will be included then, it is very much needed We have an endpoint already setup with Lodestar but we haven't made the link publicly available yet due to ddos potential as it's mostly used for dev + testing. Can provide you with a link <@687974325072035882> if you need it. I dont need it I suggest caching if you are afraid of DDOS Maybe every 2 hours you update your rpc call And just use the 2 hours old value So you wont stress the node too much Just a suggestion Mine was just a broader proposal

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: Hello, would it be feasible for the EF to start nodes for checkpoint-sync and use them for "Bootstrap nodes"?

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: I think that could improve UX by a lot as you would not need an external provider anymore

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: or is it not feasible because of DDOS or something like that?

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: I think the issue with that is more around centralization. We'd rather work on making it easier to set them up and discoverable as well as tooling to allow enough people to set them up themselves.

excerpts.author: butta
excerpts.content: afaik infura is the only checkpoint sync provider right now — added it to our todo 📝

excerpts.content: But even if it is a single provider it seems a rather hard attack on decentralization

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: My main concern is this: if we do not make it default then 90% of people running a node will run it through initial sync

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: and rightfully so as that is the default syncing method which btw is unsafe to use in the first place, so i think it would not be an attack on decentralization, quite the opposite 🙂

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: it just seems a pretty easy and impactful improvement to the UX to me anyways, which got harder already.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
keep an eye on this repo from Sam😄
https://github.com/samcm/checkpointz

The idea is for that to be a beacon node aware reverse proxy that allows just calls needed for checkpoint sync. Additionally you can configure caching to reduce the load on the node.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: that's a fair point. Our plan is to first get some tooling in place to run these nodes easily, then to make them visible and just act as a source of info. I guess we can talk about how to use that source of info once its up.
